chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about chess, so he said:
Leave the Magian thing to its people, may Allah curse it.

key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيَّةَ: The Magian thing/practice (referring to Zoroastrian origins or characteristics)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on chess in Shia Islam according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) characterized chess as 'Magian' (Majusiyyah), linking its origins and cultural adoption to the Zoroastrians, thereby associating it with religious syncretism or distinctiveness from Islamic practice. This specific descriptor elevates the ruling beyond mere leisure prohibition to a critique of its cultural roots, a view supported by later jurists who cited the game's potential to distract from remembrance of God and lead to gambling. The invocation of a curse underscores the severity of the practice in early Shia tradition, often interpreted as a strong disapproval (karahah) or prohibition (tahrim) depending on the context of use.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Ziyad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the chess, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘
Leave the Magian thing to its people, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Ziyad who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about chess. He (the Imam) said, ‘
You must leave al-Majusiayah (the Zoroastrian thing) for its people, may Allah condemn it.’”
